newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU says Anglo to cut Lonrho stake.
newsitem.headline: EU says Anglo to cut Lonrho stake.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday that South Africa's Anglo American Corp had agreed to a Commission demand to cut its stake in Lonrho Plc to 9.99 percent from 27.5 percent.
"This reduction is to be carried out within an agreed timetable should no other solution to the Commission's competition concerns be found," the EU executive said in a statement.
The Commission said it cleared Anglo American's purchase of Lonrho shares subject to the stake being cut to less than 10 percent.
It said Anglo was not required to sell its shares immediately to give it time to negotiate a sale, but that the company would transfer the shares to a trustee in the intervening period.

The Commission had expressed concern that Anglo's stake in Lonrho -- which has substantial interest in two South African platinum mines -- would put control of the world's platinum industry in the hands of Anglo and South African mining house Gencor Ltd.

"Today's decision maintains the strict application of European competition rules to the platinum sector and will permit the three South African platinum producers, Anglo, Lonrho and Gencor to continue to exist separately," the Commission said.
